name: relish
instructions:
A food-processor relish built on the pickle + mustard register: shallots, dill pickles, celery, dijon mustard, pickle juice, black pepper, optional parsley — pulsed to a coarse, spoonable relish. The hierarchy: PICKLE + CELERY > SHALLOT > PARSLEY (see notes).

MAKES ~1.5 cups. Food processor, ~10 min.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1-2 shallots, peeled and quartered
- 2-3 dill pickles, rough-chopped
- 1-2 stalks celery, rough-chopped
- (optional) a small handful of fresh parsley — secondary, see notes
- 1-2 tsp dijon mustard
- splash of pickle juice (to loosen and sharpen)
- freshly cracked black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. FOOD PROCESS: add the shallots, pickles, celery, and parsley to the food processor. Pulse to a coarse chop — relish texture, not a puree. Everything should stay in small distinct bits.
2. SEASON: add the dijon mustard, a splash of pickle juice, and black pepper. Pulse briefly to combine.
3. TASTE: adjust — more pickle juice for sharper/looser, more dijon for deeper tang. NO ADDED SALT should be needed (the pickles + juice carry it; taste first).
4. SERVE, or refrigerate — improves after an hour as the flavors merge. Keeps ~1 week.
notes:
The pickle + mustard + shallot register in condiment form — the standalone expression of the pickle-tang axis running through the anglo-germanic side of the cookbook ([[mushroom-pickle-relish]], [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]).

=== BIGGEST FAILURE MODE — TOO MUCH SHALLOT/PARSLEY ===

The biggest relish failure mode: TOO MUCH SHALLOT/PARSLEY and NOT ENOUGH PICKLE/CELERY. The hierarchy is explicit: CELERY + PICKLE are the body, the SHALLOT matters less than them, and PARSLEY matters less than the shallot (parsley is secondary — really not that important). Keep the ratio pickle-forward. (Contrast [[tartar-sauce]], where the mayo buffers the shallot and you don't have to be as shy.)

=== PULSE COARSE — RELISH, NOT PUREE ===

The food processor does the work but restraint is the technique: pulse in short bursts and stop at a coarse, even chop. Over-processing turns it into a wet slurry — the relish should be spoonable bits, not a sauce. (Same stop-early food-processor discipline as [[spinach-ricotta]]'s coarse rule.)

=== NO ADDED SALT — THE PICKLES CARRY IT ===

Same lesson as every pre-salted-ingredient dish ([[romesco]]'s canned peppers, [[basil-cottage-cheese-spread]]'s cheeses): the pickles and pickle juice bring plenty of salt. Taste before even thinking about adding more.

=== THE COMPONENTS ===

- SHALLOTS: the allium — sharper and cleaner than onion at raw-condiment scale.
- DILL PICKLES + PICKLE JUICE: the body and the acid. The juice both loosens the texture and sharpens the flavor.
- CELERY: fresh vegetal crunch against the pickles' cured crunch — two different crunches.
- PARSLEY (SECONDARY): the green freshness, but really not as important as the shallot — nice-to-have, not structural. (Fine herbs are clashing in the gravy-core lentil stews ([[creamy-french-lentils]] / [[mushroom-pickle-relish]]), but a raw condiment is a different context — parsley is welcome here, just optional.)
- DIJON: the depth-and-tang binder, in its condiment home.
- BLACK PEPPER: the only spice.

=== USES ===

- On sausages, brats, and hot dogs (the classic relish slot — german register)
- Alongside [[milk-stout-braised-beef]] or on the [[mushroom-pickle-relish]] plate — the same-register condiment
- On [[chicken-salad]] or [[egg-salad]] sandwiches
- With cold cuts, cheese boards, or a ploughman's-style plate
